audit.whatIsWrong: The two layers rendered two different level charts. content win[] reads Skill/Akshan/Galio/Galio/Galio/Akshan/Galio and matches packet.levelChart exactly; full phases[].side reads Akshan/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill and matches nothing.
audit.why: All seven rows disagree across layers. The content layer is corroborated by the packet, so the full layer is the wrong one.
audit.corrected: Proposed all seven phases[].side rows onto the content/packet verdict, with .rating and .why rewritten in the same group.

audit.whatIsWrong: The first-item row credited Galio's MR with taxing 'AP trades' — Akshan is an AD champion. tldr, winCon and report[0]/report[1] all called him an AP assassin.
audit.why: Avengerang, the passive double shot and Comeuppance are physical damage; MR buys nothing in this lane.
audit.corrected: Rewrote those fields around AD, and made the first-item row say why the item swing favours him.

audit.whatIsWrong: Six fields claimed Comeuppance (R) revives allies. It does not — Going Rogue (W) resurrects, and only when Akshan kills the Scoundrel who killed them. wants.foe[1] also used a fabricated name, 'Avengeance'.
audit.why: Riot's text: Comeuppance stores bullets and deals missing-health damage to the first target hit. The resurrection is entirely on W.
audit.corrected: Fixed every instance, and stated the decisive interaction the page never had: Heroic Swing knocks him off when he collides with a champion, so your E-knockup and your body both end the arc.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns held no digit at all.
audit.why: It is the field that carries real numbers.
audit.corrected: Heroic Swing 18s at rank 1 down to 12s at rank 5, Avengerang 9s at rank 1, against your 650-range E.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two copy-paste bleeds (dosFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d carried the trade strings under unrelated titles) plus the no-digit cooldowns field.

edits.before: - Akshan Heroic Swing: matchup-defining — His swing engage/escape — fight only while it is down. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget W Shield of Durand for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Heroic Swing is 18s at rank 1 and 12s at rank 5 — it is his engage and his only escape, so step up on its downtime. - Avengerang is 9s at rank 1; with both down he cannot leave your 650 E.

edits.before: His swing engage/escape — fight only while it is down. Its cooldown is the green light — wait for it.
edits.after: Heroic Swing is his engage and his escape on one 18s bar — fight while it is down and he cannot leave.

edits.before: Q the contact, let the tornado tick, E-auto if he answers, W-taunt the commit — a full rotation where his half landed on a shield.
edits.after: When he swings out, Q the ground where the arc ends rather than where he stood — the tornado ticks on him as he drops off the hook.

edits.before: That’s Akshan’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: He can jump off the swing early — release the taunt on the landing, not the arc.

edits.before: Charging W through a minion line at a mage holding his answer — the statue mid-charge is the lane's easiest skillshot target.
edits.after: Justice Punch is 11s at rank 1 and it is how you answer a swing — roam without it and he takes the wave and a plate.

edits.before: Ahead, tax both maps: zone Akshan with taunt threat, keep the wave middle, and R every skirmish — fed Galio makes the enemy jungler unemployed.
edits.after: Ahead, deny the reset: Going Rogue only pays him if he kills the Scoundrel, so keep your team's deaths clean and R every skirmish he shows up to.

edits.before: Carry through arrivals — Hero's Entrance turns every losing skirmish your team starts into a 5v4 with a knockup.
edits.after: Carry by arriving: R shields the ally and knocks up — land it on whoever he swung onto and his arc ends early.

edits.before: Level 6: Akshan's global revive ultimate gives him more raw impact potential in skirmishes.
edits.after: Level 6: Comeuppance stores bullets and hits harder the lower you are, giving him kill reach.

edits.before: Akshan's Comeuppance can revive an ally and turn a fight instantly, so hold Hero's Entrance for when he's on cooldown or bait it out before engaging.
edits.after: Comeuppance revives nobody — Going Rogue does that, and only when he kills whoever killed his ally, so denying that kill matters more than baiting his ult.

edits.before: You out-scale as a frontline that can engage through his stealth windows, but his global ult means your team must clean up kills fast before he revives someone.
edits.after: You out-scale as a frontline that engages through his camouflage windows, but every Scoundrel he kills brings a dead ally back with Going Rogue — deny that reset.

edits.before: From level 3 onward your combo out-trades his auto-reliant kit, and by 6 you need to respect that his ultimate can revive a dying ally across the map — bait it before all-in-ing. Play around his cooldowns rather than his damage once you're ahead.
edits.after: From level 3 onward your combo out-trades his auto-reliant kit, and Heroic Swing at 18s on rank 1 is the cooldown that decides everything — without it he cannot leave. His revive comes off Going Rogue killing a Scoundrel, not off his ultimate.

edits.before: You become the stronger teamfight piece thanks to your engage and durability, but his Comeuppance means your team must focus fire and clean up kills quickly before he can turn a loss into a stalemate.
edits.after: You become the stronger teamfight piece thanks to your engage and durability, but Comeuppance deals more the lower its target is — peel your low carries out of its 2500 range instead of trading into it.

edits.before: Bait Comeuppance before committing your own engage in skirmishes
edits.after: Engage only while Heroic Swing is down — it is his one escape

edits.before: Pick off a squishy backline pick with Avengeance and camouflage
edits.after: Pick off a squishy with Avengerang out of a camouflage approach

edits.before: Save Comeuppance to revive a dying ally and swing a teamfight
edits.after: Kill whoever killed his ally to resurrect them with Going Rogue

notes: The chart edits here are UNPAIRED BY NECESSITY: content win[0..6] already matches packet.levelChart, and it was the full-layer phases[].side that was wrong on all seven rows. Since win[N] is already correct there is no before/after pair to propose for it — an edit whose before equals its after is not a valid edit. All seven side rows plus their ratings and whys are proposed as one atomic group; after it lands the two layers agree for the first time. If the applier's rule refuses a side edit with no win[N] twin, this whole chart stays broken and needs the user's call (see questionsForUser). Separately: report[3].t still carries the old trade strings that I rewrote elsewhere, but the report cap of two rewrites per matchup was spent on report[0] and report[1], both of which stated the outright falsehood that Akshan is an AP assassin.
